report.source_text: Three months after the trauma, the macular condition remained unchanged. Subsequently, the patient was referred to the vitreoretinal surgeon, who performed pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling using the inverted flap technique and 20% SF6 gas tamponade.

report.source_text: OCT imaging (Fig. 3, 4) showed a closed macular defect and residual postoperative tissue reorganization. The best-corrected visual acuity improved to 0.3 three months postoperatively.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old presented with sudden vision decrease in the right eye after blunt trauma. Initial exam showed hyphema, corneal edema, and post-traumatic uveitis signs. Indirect fundoscopy and optical coherence tomography (OCT) on admission confirmed a full-thickness macular rupture. Vision remained poor (BCVA 0.02) with stable macular rupture at two months. At three months post-trauma, pars plana vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling and gas tamponade was performed. Postoperative OCT showed closure of the macular defect with residual tissue reorganization and BCVA improved to 0.3 three months after surgery.
